gaps.sentence: The ___ issue of the magazine has an interview with the president.
gaps.explanation: 'Current' means happening or existing now; 'actual' means real as opposed to possible or estimated.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to choose ___ the two options.
gaps.explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for a group of more than two.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
She sat ___ me during the whole flight.
gaps.explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.hint: you ___ a match, but ___ the other team
gaps.explanation: 'Win' takes the game or prize as object (win a match); 'beat/defeat' take the opponent as object.

gaps.sentence: I ___ seeing that man somewhere before.
Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.
